# couchbase-capella_eventing_function (Resource)

Manages an eventing function on a Capella cluster, including its JavaScript code, source and metadata keyspaces, runtime settings, bindings, and deployment state.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) The GUID4 ID of the cluster.
- `event_metadata_storage` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--event_metadata_storage))
- `event_source` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--event_source))
- `name` (String) - The name of the eventing function.
 - **Constraints**: Minimum length: 1 characters, Maximum length: 100 characters, Pattern: `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*$`
- `organization_id` (String) The GUID4 ID of the organization.
- `project_id` (String) The GUID4 ID of the project.

### Optional

- `bindings` (Attributes) - A binding is a construct that lets you separate environment-specific variables, like keyspace names, external endpoint URLs and credentials, and global constants, from the source code of the Eventing Function. A binding provides indirection between environment-specific artifacts and symbolic names, and helps move a function definition from a development to a production environment without changing the eventing code. Binding names must be valid JavaScript identifiers, and cannot conflict with built-in types. An Eventing Function can have no bindings, one binding, or several bindings. Aliases must be unique across all three binding types. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bindings))
- `code` (String, Sensitive) - The JavaScript code of the eventing function that gets executed in response to document mutations.
- `description` (String) - The eventing function description.
- `settings` (Attributes) - Runtime settings that control how the function is executed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--settings))
- `state` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--event_metadata_storage"></a>
### Nested Schema for `event_metadata_storage`

Required:

- `bucket` (String) - The name of the bucket.
 - **Constraints**: Minimum length: 1 characters, Maximum length: 100 characters, Pattern: `^[a-zA-Z0-9_%-][a-zA-Z0-9._%-]*$`

Optional:

- `collection` (String) A specific collection denoted by the App Endpoint name, the scope name and collection name separated by a period, for example "endpoint1.scope1.collection1".
If only an App Endpoint name is provided this will be interpreted as "endpoint1._default._default". If only an App Endpoint name and collection name are

- `scope` (String) A specific collection denoted by the App Endpoint name, the scope name and collection name separated by a period, for example "endpoint1.scope1.collection1".
If only an App Endpoint name is provided this will be interpreted as "endpoint1._default._default". If only an App Endpoint name and collection name are
provided these will interpreted as a named collection within the default scope, for example "endpoint1.collection1" will be interpreted as "endpoint1._default.collection1".

<a id="nestedatt--bindings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bindings`

Optional:

- `buckets` (Attributes List) - Bucket bindings that give the eventing function direct access to documents in a collection. A wildcard value of `*` can be used for the bucket, scope or collection to give the eventing function access to multiple keyspaces. A wildcard must cascade down the hierarchy: a wildcard bucket requires a wildcard scope and collection, and a wildcard scope requires a wildcard collection. In this case, only the [Advanced Keyspace Accessors](https://docs.couchbase.com/cloud/eventing/eventing-advanced-keyspace-accessors.html) can read or write to the bucket from the eventing function code. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bindings--buckets))
- `constants` (Attributes List) - Constant bindings that expose a fixed value to the eventing function code as a global variable. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bindings--constants))
- `urls` (Attributes List) - URL bindings that the eventing function can use to access external resources. Each binding specifies the endpoint, the HTTP or HTTPS protocol, and the credentials used to authenticate with the remote host. URL bindings can be used by the `curl` function in the eventing function code. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bindings--urls))

<a id="nestedatt--bindings--buckets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bindings.buckets`

Required:

- `alias` (String) - The name used to refer to the bound collection from the eventing function code.
 - **Constraints**: Minimum length: 1 characters, Maximum length: 64 characters, Pattern: `^[a-zA-Z_$][a-zA-Z0-9_$]*$`
- `bucket` (String) - The name of the bucket that the alias resolves to. Can be a wildcard value of `*` to give the eventing function access to all buckets. When the bucket is `*`, the scope and collection must also be `*`.
 - **Constraints**: Minimum length: 1 characters, Maximum length: 100 characters, Pattern: `^(\*|[a-zA-Z0-9_%-][a-zA-Z0-9._%-]*)$`

Optional:

- `collection` (String) A specific collection denoted by the App Endpoint name, the scope name and collection name separated by a period, for example "endpoint1.scope1.collection1".
If only an App Endpoint name is provided this will be interpreted as "endpoint1._default._default". If only an App Endpoint name and collection name are
provided these will interpreted as a named collection within the default scope, for example "endpoint1.collection1" will be interpreted as "endpoint1._default.collection1".
- `permission` (String) - The level of access the eventing function has on the bound collection. `read`: the eventing function can read documents from the collection but cannot create, update, or delete them. `readWrite`: the eventing function can read documents from, and write documents to, the collection.
 - **Valid Values**: `read`, `readWrite`
 - **Default**: `read`
- `scope` (String) A specific collection denoted by the App Endpoint name, the scope name and collection name separated by a period, for example "endpoint1.scope1.collection1".
If only an App Endpoint name is provided this will be interpreted as "endpoint1._default._default". If only an App Endpoint name and collection name are
provided these will interpreted as a named collection within the default scope, for example "endpoint1.collection1" will be interpreted as "endpoint1._default.collection1".


<a id="nestedatt--bindings--constants"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bindings.constants`

Required:

- `alias` (String) - The global variable name under which the value is exposed to the eventing function code.
 - **Constraints**: Minimum length: 1 characters, Maximum length: 64 characters, Pattern: `^[a-zA-Z_$][a-zA-Z0-9_$]*$`
- `value` (String) - The literal value the alias resolves to when referenced from the eventing function code.
 - **Constraints**: Minimum length: 1 characters


<a id="nestedatt--bindings--urls"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bindings.urls`

Required:

- `alias` (String) - The name used to refer to the bound endpoint from the eventing function code.
 - **Constraints**: Minimum length: 1 characters, Maximum length: 64 characters, Pattern: `^[a-zA-Z_$][a-zA-Z0-9_$]*$`
- `url` (String) - The fully qualified endpoint URL, including the HTTP or HTTPS scheme, that requests are sent to.
 - **Constraints**: Pattern: `^https?:\/\/`
 - **Format**: URI

Optional:

- `allow_cookies` (Boolean) - Whether the eventing function should allow cookies on the session.
 - **Default**: `false`
- `authentication` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bindings--urls--authentication))
- `validate_tls_certificate` (Boolean)

<a id="nestedatt--bindings--urls--authentication"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bindings.urls.authentication`

Required:

- `type` (String)

Optional:

- `bearer_token` (String, Sensitive)
- `password` (String, Sensitive)
- `username` (String)




<a id="nestedatt--settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `settings`

Optional:

- `allow_sync_documents` (Boolean) - Determines whether the function is permitted to process mutations on documents managed by App Services. When set to `false`, documents prefixed with `_sync` are skipped. Set `allowSyncDocuments` to `false` and `cursorAware` to `true` for App Services compatibility.
 - **Default**: `true`
- `cursor_aware` (Boolean) - When `true`, the function suppresses potential duplicate mutations originating from App Services, guaranteeing that the eventing function is invoked at most once per logical mutation. Set `allowSyncDocuments` to `false` and `cursorAware` to `true` for App Services compatibility. A maximum of 5 cursor-aware eventing functions can be deployed against a single source keyspace; deploying a cursor-aware function beyond this limit is rejected.
 - **Default**: `false`
- `feed_boundary` (String) - The position at which the eventing function starts processing mutations when it is first deployed. Note that an eventing function is created in an `undeployed` state, and does not start processing mutations until it is deployed. `everything`: process the entire history of mutations on the source collection. `from_now`: only process mutations that occur after the function is deployed.
 - **Valid Values**: `everything`, `from_now`
 - **Default**: `from_now`
- `language_compatibility` (String) - The language version of the Eventing Function for backward compatibility. This ensures that when a cluster is upgraded, existing functions continue to operate without modification. When a new language version is released, functions can be migrated to it to take advantage of new features and improvements.
 - **Valid Values**: `6.0.0`, `6.5.0`, `6.6.2`, `7.2.0`
 - **Default**: `7.2.0`
- `max_timer_context_size` (Number) - The maximum size, in bytes, of the context object that can be attached to a Timer created by the Eventing Function. A context can be any JSON document. Timers can store and access a context, which is then used to store the state of when a Timer is created and to retrieve the state of when a Timer is fired.
 - **Constraints**: Minimum: 20, Maximum: 2.097152e+07
 - **Default**: `1024`
- `script_timeout` (Number) - The maximum duration, in seconds, that a single invocation (from start to finish) of the eventing function is permitted to run before it is terminated.
 - **Constraints**: Minimum: 1
 - **Default**: `60`
- `sql_consistency` (String) - The consistency level used by SQL++ (N1QL) statements executed from within the eventing function. `none`: queries execute without waiting for any specific indexer state. `request`: queries wait for indexes to incorporate all mutations made up to the time the query was issued.
 - **Valid Values**: `none`, `request`
 - **Default**: `none`
- `worker_count` (Number) - The number of worker processes the function uses on each Eventing node. Increasing this value can improve throughput at the cost of additional CPU and memory consumption.
 - **Constraints**: Minimum: 1, Maximum: 64
 - **Default**: `1`

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import couchbase-capella_eventing_function.new_eventing_function function_name=<function_name>,cluster_id=<cluster_id>,project_id=<project_id>,organization_id=<organization_id>
```
